questions.prompt: You map www.example.com to an App Service app and want DNS to follow its default hostname rather than a fixed IP. Which routing record does Microsoft recommend?

options.text: A CNAME from www to the app default hostname.
options.explanation: CNAME maps the subdomain to the hostname.

options.text: A TXT record containing only the app IP.
options.explanation: TXT verification is not traffic routing.

options.text: An MX record targeting the app hostname.
options.explanation: MX controls mail delivery, not web traffic resolution.

options.text: An NS record delegating www to the app hostname.
options.explanation: An app hostname is not an authoritative DNS nameserver.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the asuid.www TXT record when configuring www.example.com for App Service?

options.text: Prove domain ownership and help prevent another app claiming the hostname.
options.explanation: The domain verification ID supports ownership verification and takeover protection.

options.text: Route HTTPS packets to the app private IP.
options.explanation: TXT records do not route client traffic.

options.text: Store the certificate private key for browsers.
options.explanation: A public TXT record must not contain a private key.

options.text: Set the App Service plan worker count.
options.explanation: DNS verification does not configure compute capacity.

questions.prompt: www.example.com resolves to the correct App Service address, but the app has no custom-hostname entry for it and requests return a platform 404. What should be configured?

options.text: Validate and add the hostname binding to the intended app.
options.explanation: App Service must associate that Host header with the app.

options.text: Only lower the DNS TTL repeatedly.
options.explanation: Correct resolution cannot replace the missing app mapping.

options.text: Only add another identical A record.
options.explanation: Duplicating routing does not establish the hostname binding.
Additional workers do not register the custom hostname.
